description: Standalone Kubernetes resource management desktop application with tree navigation and resource views.

tech_stack.notes: Use electron-vite for Electron + Vite integration. Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite plugin. shadcn/ui components copied into src/renderer/components/ui/. Main process handles kubeconfig and k8s API calls via IPC; renderer is the React UI.

architecture.main_process: Reads ~/.kube/config, creates k8s API clients, exposes IPC handlers for resource queries
architecture.renderer_process: React app with Tailwind layout: left tree view + right resource panel. shadcn/ui components for Table, Sheet, Badge, Collapsible.
architecture.ipc_pattern: renderer calls ipcRenderer.invoke('k8s:<resource>:<action>', ...args), main process returns serialized data

stories.title: Project scaffold with Electron + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn
stories.description: Initialize the project using the official electron-vite scaffold: run `npm create @quick-start/electron@latest . -- --template react-ts` in the project root (the dot targets the current directory). Then: (1) Install Tailwind CSS v4 via `npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite` and add the Vite plugin to electron.vite.config.ts renderer config. (2) Add `@import 'tailwindcss'` to src/renderer/assets/main.css. (3) Configure shadcn by creating components.json manually (do NOT run npx shadcn init as it misdetects the electron-vite structure). The components.json should set aliases pointing to src/renderer/. (4) Install shadcn peer deps: `npm install class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react @radix-ui/react-collapsible @radix-ui/react-slot`. (5) Install remaining packages from key_packages. The app should launch and show a blank window.
acceptance_criteria: npm install completes without errors
npm run dev starts the Electron app
A blank Electron window opens successfully
TypeScript compiles without errors
Tailwind utility classes apply correctly in the renderer

stories.title: kind cluster setup script and test fixture manifests
stories.description: Create a local testing environment using kind (Kubernetes IN Docker). Provide: (1) a shell script `scripts/setup-kind.sh` that creates a kind cluster named 'innfiswindow-test', waits for it to be ready, and applies test fixture manifests. (2) A directory `scripts/fixtures/` containing YAML manifests that exercise every resource type the app supports: at least 2 namespaces (test-ns-1, test-ns-2), 1 deployment (nginx, 2 replicas), 1 statefulset (a simple single-replica postgres-like app), 1 daemonset (a log-collector DaemonSet using a pause image with tolerations), 2 configmaps (one with multiple keys including a multi-line value), 1 secret (Opaque type with 2 keys), and 1 node (kind provides this automatically — no manifest needed). (3) A teardown script `scripts/teardown-kind.sh` that deletes the cluster. The setup script must be idempotent: if the cluster already exists, it skips creation. Include a `scripts/README.md` explaining prerequisites (kind, kubectl), how to run setup/teardown, and how to point the app at the kind context (`kind-innfiswindow-test`).
acceptance_criteria: scripts/setup-kind.sh creates a kind cluster named 'innfiswindow-test' (idempotent)
scripts/fixtures/ contains manifests covering: namespaces, deployment, statefulset, daemonset, configmaps, secrets
After running setup, kubectl get all -A shows all fixture workloads running
scripts/teardown-kind.sh deletes the kind cluster cleanly
scripts/README.md documents prerequisites and usage
stories.notes: kind config should set a single control-plane node. Use lightweight images (nginx:alpine, pause:3.9, busybox) to keep pull times short. All fixture manifests go into namespace test-ns-1 or test-ns-2 except cluster-scoped resources.

stories.title: IPC handler integration tests against kind cluster
stories.description: Write integration tests for every IPC handler in the main process, executed against the kind cluster created in S15. Use Vitest (already a dev dep via electron-vite) with a test file at `src/main/__tests__/k8s-handlers.integration.test.ts`. Each test should: import and call the handler function directly (not via IPC), pointing KubeConfig at the 'kind-innfiswindow-test' context. Test file must check the KUBECONFIG env var or default kubeconfig for the kind context — if not found, skip all tests with `test.skipIf`. Handlers to test: k8s:contexts:list, k8s:context:current, k8s:namespaces:list, k8s:nodes:list, k8s:deployments:list, k8s:pods:list, k8s:replicasets:list, k8s:statefulsets:list, k8s:daemonsets:list, k8s:configmaps:list, k8s:secrets:list. For each: assert the result is an array, verify at least one item from the fixture manifests appears (check by name), and assert required fields are present on each item.
acceptance_criteria: Test file at src/main/__tests__/k8s-handlers.integration.test.ts
All 11 IPC handlers have at least one integration test
Tests skip gracefully when kind context 'kind-innfiswindow-test' is not available
Each test asserts: result is an array, expected fixture resource appears by name, required fields are non-null
npm run test (or npx vitest run) executes the tests without hanging
stories.notes: Refactor main-process handler logic into exported functions so tests can import them directly without spinning up the full Electron app. Tests run in Node environment (not jsdom). Add a vitest.config.ts or configure in package.json if not already present.

stories.title: Create, update, and delete deployments
stories.description: Add full CRUD support for Deployments. Users can create a new deployment via a form dialog, edit an existing deployment's replica count and container image via an edit dialog, and delete a deployment with a confirmation prompt. All mutations go through IPC handlers in the main process using AppsV1Api. The Deployments list refreshes automatically after any mutation.
acceptance_criteria: IPC handler `k8s:deployment:create` accepts namespace, name, image, and replicas; creates the deployment and returns the created object
IPC handler `k8s:deployment:update` accepts namespace, name, image, and replicas; patches the deployment and returns the updated object
IPC handler `k8s:deployment:delete` accepts namespace and name; deletes the deployment and returns a success status
A 'New Deployment' button in the Deployments list view opens a modal form with fields: name, namespace (dropdown from loaded namespaces), image, replicas
Each row in the Deployments table has an Edit button that opens a pre-filled edit dialog for image and replicas
Each row in the Deployments table has a Delete button that shows a confirmation dialog before deleting
After create, update, or delete the deployment list re-fetches and the UI updates
Errors from the k8s API are surfaced to the user in the dialog (not silently swallowed)
stories.notes: Use `appsV1Api.createNamespacedDeployment` for create, `appsV1Api.patchNamespacedDeployment` with a strategic merge patch for update, and `appsV1Api.deleteNamespacedDeployment` for delete. Dialogs should use shadcn Dialog + Form components. Keep the form minimal — name, namespace, image, replicas are sufficient.

After create, update, or delete the Ingress list re-fetches and the UI updates
Errors from the k8s API are surfaced to the user in the dialog (not silently swallowed)
stories.notes: Use `networkingV1Api.createNamespacedIngress` for create, `networkingV1Api.patchNamespacedIngress` with a strategic merge patch for update, and `networkingV1Api.deleteNamespacedIngress` for delete. The rules form should support adding/removing multiple rule rows. pathType must be one of 'Prefix', 'Exact', or 'ImplementationSpecific'. servicePort in the rule backend can be a number (port number) — use `{number: portValue}` in the IntOrString field. Dialogs should use shadcn Dialog + Form components.

stories.title: YAML editor for resource create and update
stories.description: Add a full-featured YAML editor panel that activates when users create or update any Kubernetes resource. Instead of (or alongside) form-based dialogs, users can write or edit raw YAML for any resource kind and apply it via a generic `k8s:resource:apply` IPC handler. The editor should provide syntax highlighting, basic YAML validation, and clear error feedback. This replaces the per-resource form dialogs as the primary create/edit mechanism for power users who prefer working directly with YAML manifests.
acceptance_criteria: A `YamlEditorPanel` component is created at `src/renderer/components/YamlEditorPanel.tsx` using Monaco Editor (`@monaco-editor/react`) configured for YAML language mode with syntax highlighting

IPC handler `k8s:resource:apply` accepts a YAML string, parses it to a k8s object (apiVersion, kind, metadata.namespace, metadata.name), and performs create-or-update using `KubernetesObjectApi` (try create first; on 409 Conflict, patch with strategic merge); returns the applied object

Each resource list view (Deployments, Pods, Services, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, Secrets) gains an 'Edit YAML' button per row that opens `YamlEditorPanel` pre-populated with the resource's current YAML (serialized via `js-yaml`)
Each resource list view gains a 'New Resource (YAML)' button that opens `YamlEditorPanel` with a starter template for that resource kind
The editor panel has an 'Apply' button that calls `k8s:resource:apply` and closes the panel on success; errors are shown inline below the editor
YAML is validated client-side (via `js-yaml` parse) before the IPC call; syntax errors are shown immediately without a round-trip to the main process
The panel is displayed as a modal dialog (shadcn Dialog) with a minimum height of 60vh and a monospace font editor area
After a successful apply the affected resource list re-fetches and the UI updates
stories.notes: Use `@monaco-editor/react` for the editor (install `@monaco-editor/react` and `monaco-editor`). Use `js-yaml` (already likely present) to serialize existing resources to YAML for pre-population and to parse user input before the IPC call. For `KubernetesObjectApi`, use `KubernetesObjectApi.makeApiClient(kc)` then call `.create(obj)` on success path and `.patch(obj, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/strategic-merge-patch+json' } })` on conflict. Starter templates should include the minimal required fields (apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec). The 'Edit YAML' button should be added to existing table rows without removing the existing per-resource form-based Edit/Delete buttons.

stories.title: Architecture audit and refactoring plan
stories.description: Analyse the current codebase structure, measure key architectural health signals, and produce a written refactoring plan. The output is a markdown report at `docs/architecture-refactor-plan.md`. The agent must read every file under `src/` (main, preload, renderer), measure the signals listed below, identify the top pain-points, and propose concrete, prioritised refactoring actions — each with rationale, affected files, and estimated complexity (S/M/L). No production code is changed in this story.
acceptance_criteria: File `docs/architecture-refactor-plan.md` exists and is committed

Report section 'Current State' lists: total file count, lines of code per layer (main / preload / renderer), number of IPC handlers, number of Zustand store slices, number of React components, and any files exceeding 300 LOC
Report section 'Pain Points' identifies at least 5 concrete issues (e.g. handler co-location, missing error boundary layer, store shape, component granularity, test coverage gaps, IPC type-safety)
Report section 'Refactoring Plan' contains prioritised actions (P1/P2/P3), each with: description, motivation, affected files or directories, and complexity estimate
Report section 'Proposed Directory Layout' shows a tree of the recommended future `src/` structure after refactoring
Report is written in clear technical prose — no vague recommendations like 'improve code quality'; every suggestion names specific files or patterns
stories.notes: This is an analysis-only story. The agent should use Read/Glob/Grep tools to gather metrics, then Write the report. Do not refactor any code. Complexity estimates: S = hours, M = 1-2 days, L = 3+ days. The plan should be actionable enough that another agent can pick up any P1 item and implement it without further design work.

stories.title: Color palette preset switcher
stories.description: Add a color palette preset system that lets users switch between named themes at runtime. Five presets are defined — Default, Ocean, Midnight, Slate, and Cyberpunk — each providing a complete set of shadcn/ui CSS variable overrides for both light and dark modes. The active preset is stored in Zustand and persisted to localStorage; switching a preset applies immediately without a page reload by writing CSS variables onto the document root. A preset picker is accessible from the AppBar.
acceptance_criteria: A `src/renderer/lib/themes.ts` file exports a `Theme` type and a `THEMES` constant — an array of 5 preset objects, each with: `id` (string), `name` (string), `light` (CSS variable map), and `dark` (CSS variable map). The 5 presets are: Default (zinc-based neutrals), Ocean (blue/cyan, trust-inducing DevOps feel), Midnight (deep navy + indigo accents, Stripe-like), Slate (muted cool grays, minimal professional), and Cyberpunk (neon green/cyan on near-black, terminal aesthetic). Each preset defines at minimum these tokens: --background, --foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --primary, --primary-foreground, --secondary, --secondary-foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --accent, --accent-foreground, --destructive, --border, --ring
Color values are expressed in oklch format (e.g. `oklch(0.145 0 0)`) to align with Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui conventions

A `applyTheme(themeId: string, mode: 'light' | 'dark')` function in `src/renderer/lib/themes.ts` writes the preset's CSS variable map onto `document.documentElement` style; it is called on mount and on every preset or mode change
The Zustand store (`src/renderer/store/app.store.ts`) gains a `themeId` field (default `'default'`) with `setThemeId` action; the value is persisted to localStorage via `zustand/middleware` `persist`

A `ThemePicker` component at `src/renderer/components/ThemePicker.tsx` renders as a palette icon button in the AppBar that opens a shadcn Popover listing all 5 presets as clickable color swatches (showing the preset's primary color); the active preset is highlighted with a ring
Clicking a swatch in `ThemePicker` calls `setThemeId`, which triggers `applyTheme` via a `useEffect` in the root `App.tsx`

On app startup, the persisted `themeId` and the current dark/light OS preference (via `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`) are read and `applyTheme` is called before first render to avoid a flash of unstyled content
The existing dark mode toggle (if present) continues to work; toggling dark/light re-applies the active preset in the new mode

stories.title: Resource detail panel toggle and close button
stories.description: Clicking a resource row that is already selected should deselect it (toggle behaviour), collapsing the detail panel. A close button (X) must appear in the top-right corner of the detail panel so users can dismiss it without clicking the row again.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a resource row when it is already the selected item calls `setSelectedItem(null)`, which collapses the detail panel
Clicking a different row still selects that row as before

Every resource detail panel (Namespaces, Nodes, Deployments, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Pods, Services, Ingresses) renders a close button (an X icon button) in the top-right corner of the panel header

stories.title: Resource detail panel vivid card background
stories.description: The resource detail panel currently blends into the background because the card colour is too close to the page background. stories.title: YAML editor panel theme integration
stories.description: The YAML / text editor panel (YamlEditorPanel) used for viewing and editing resource manifests does not respect the active colour theme. stories.title: Custom scrollbar styling
stories.description: All scrollable containers in the app currently show the OS default scrollbar, which does not match the app's visual design. Apply a consistent custom scrollbar style to all scrollable areas (sidebar tree, resource list, detail panels, editor) that complements the active theme.

The scrollbar width is narrower than the OS default (e.g. 6–8 px) and the thumb has rounded corners

Delete buttons and Create buttons remain unaffected

stories.title: Global error snackbar for IPC and runtime errors
stories.description: Add a global error-handling layer that captures errors from IPC calls (k8s API failures, kubeconfig issues, etc.) and runtime errors in the renderer, then displays them as a dismissible snackbar/toast notification at the bottom of the screen. All existing resource view components (Deployments, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, Services, Pods, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ReplicaSets, Nodes, Namespaces) must route their caught errors through this system instead of silently dropping them.
acceptance_criteria: A `useToast` hook and `Toaster` component from shadcn/ui (sonner or the built-in toast) are installed and rendered once in the root App component
A shared `handleIpcError(err: unknown, context: string)` utility (e.g. in `src/renderer/lib/ipc-error.ts`) calls `toast.error(...)` with the error message and optional context label

Every resource view component (Deployments, DaemonSets, StatefulSets, Services, Pods, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ReplicaSets, Nodes, Namespaces) wraps its IPC calls in try/catch and calls `handleIpcError` on failure instead of console.error or silent failure
The snackbar appears at the bottom-right (or bottom-center) of the screen and is dismissible by clicking
The snackbar auto-dismisses after 5 seconds
Multiple errors queue correctly — each error shows as its own toast
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Use the shadcn/ui Sonner integration (`sonner` package + `<Toaster />` from `sonner`) for the toast. Copy `src/renderer/components/ui/sonner.tsx` as the shadcn wrapper. Add `sonner` to package.json dependencies.

stories.title: Pod log tailing panel
stories.description: Add a live log-tailing panel for pods. When a user selects a pod row in PodsView and clicks a new 'Logs' button, a log panel opens (replacing or alongside the detail panel) that streams the pod's container logs in real time using the Kubernetes log-follow API. The panel shows a scrollable, auto-scrolling text area of log lines and has a Stop/Close control.
acceptance_criteria: A 'Logs' button (e.g. ScrollText icon from lucide-react) appears in each pod row in PodsView, alongside the existing YAML and Delete buttons
Clicking the Logs button opens a `PodLogPanel` component in the right-hand detail area, replacing any previously open detail or YAML panel for that pod

The main process registers an IPC channel `k8s:pod:log:start` that accepts `{ namespace, podName, containerName? }` and begins streaming logs using `@kubernetes/client-node` `CoreV1Api.readNamespacedPodLog` with `follow: true` and `tailLines: 200`
Log lines are forwarded to the renderer via `webContents.send` on a channel `k8s:pod:log:data` as plain strings
A second IPC channel `k8s:pod:log:stop` accepts `{ namespace, podName }` and aborts the active stream for that pod
The `PodLogPanel` component subscribes to `k8s:pod:log:data` events, appends lines to state, and auto-scrolls to the bottom unless the user has manually scrolled up
The panel has a 'Stop' button that calls `k8s:pod:log:stop` and a 'Close' button that also stops the stream and hides the panel
Log text is rendered in a monospace font in a dark background area; each line is displayed verbatim
If the pod has multiple containers, a dropdown lets the user select the container; changing container restarts the stream
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
ipc_handlers: k8s:pod:log:start — starts log stream for a pod/container; sends lines via webContents.send('k8s:pod:log:data', line)
k8s:pod:log:stop — aborts the active log stream for the given pod
stories.notes: Use the `@kubernetes/client-node` `Log` class (`import { Log } from '@kubernetes/client-node'`) with a PassThrough or Writable stream to receive lines. Store active streams in a Map in the main process keyed by `${namespace}/${podName}` so they can be aborted. Expose `window.api.startPodLog`, `window.api.stopPodLog`, and `window.api.onPodLogData` through the preload contextBridge.

stories.title: Add close button to Toaster notifications
stories.description: The Toaster component (`src/renderer/components/ui/sonner.tsx`) currently renders toast notifications without a visible close (X) button. Update the Toaster configuration so each toast shows a close button that the user can click to immediately dismiss it, in addition to the existing auto-dismiss behaviour.

A visible close (X) button appears on each toast notification
Clicking the close button immediately dismisses the toast

No TypeScript compile errors after the changes

stories.title: Kubernetes Events resource view with live tail
stories.description: Add Events as a new resource type. The left-hand tree view gains an 'Events' entry under a new or existing section. Selecting it shows an EventsView table listing recent events cluster-wide (or filtered by namespace). Each event row shows Type, Reason, Object, Message, Count, and Last Seen. A 'Tail' toggle button at the top of the view starts live-watching for new events and appends them to the list in real time, similar to the pod log tail feature.
acceptance_criteria: The tree view sidebar gains an 'Events' item (e.g. under a 'Cluster' or 'Workloads' section); clicking it sets the active view to 'events'
An `EventsView` component is created at `src/renderer/src/components/EventsView.tsx` that fetches and displays events in a table
The table columns are: Type (Normal/Warning badge), Reason, Involved Object (kind/name), Namespace, Message (truncated), Count, Last Seen (age-formatted timestamp)
Warning-type events are visually distinguished (e.g. amber/yellow row tint or badge)
The main process registers `k8s:events:list` IPC handler that calls `CoreV1Api.listEventForAllNamespaces` (or `listNamespacedEvent` when a namespace is selected) and returns serialized event objects

A 'Tail' toggle button at the top of EventsView starts/stops live watching via a new IPC channel `k8s:events:watch:start` / `k8s:events:watch:stop`; new events are pushed to the renderer via `webContents.send('k8s:events:data', event)`
While tailing, new events are prepended or appended to the list (newest first preferred) and the list is capped at 500 entries to prevent memory growth
Stopping the tail or navigating away calls `k8s:events:watch:stop` to clean up the watch stream
Errors from IPC calls are routed through `handleIpcError` (from S33)

ipc_handlers: k8s:events:list — lists events (all namespaces or filtered); returns plain serialized array
k8s:events:watch:start — begins a k8s watch on events; pushes new events via webContents.send('k8s:events:data', event)
k8s:events:watch:stop — aborts the active events watch stream
stories.notes: Use `CoreV1Api.listEventForAllNamespaces` with `watch: true` via the `@kubernetes/client-node` `Watch` helper class for the tail feature. Expose `window.api.listEvents`, `window.api.startEventsWatch`, `window.api.stopEventsWatch`, and `window.api.onEventsData` through the preload contextBridge. Age-format timestamps using a simple helper (e.g. '2m ago', '1h ago').

stories.title: Bottom drawer panel with New resource button and YAML editor
stories.description: Add a persistent bottom drawer panel to the main layout. The drawer has a toolbar at its top edge containing a 'New' button. Clicking 'New' opens the existing YAML editor (YamlEditorPanel or equivalent) inside the drawer, pre-populated with an empty resource template, allowing the user to author and apply a new Kubernetes resource from scratch via `k8s:resource:apply`.
acceptance_criteria: A bottom drawer panel is rendered in the main App layout, below the tree-view / resource-list split area; it is always visible as a slim toolbar (e.g. 32px tall) and can be expanded
The drawer toolbar contains a 'New' button (e.g. Plus icon from lucide-react) on its left side and a collapse/expand toggle on its right side

Clicking 'New' expands the drawer (if collapsed) and renders the YAML editor inside it, pre-filled with a minimal Kubernetes resource skeleton (apiVersion, kind, metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec: {})
The YAML editor inside the drawer reuses the existing `YamlEditorPanel` component (or the same Monaco editor integration) — no duplicate editor implementation
The drawer has a configurable height (default ~40% of window height) and the user can resize it by dragging the top edge
An 'Apply' button (or the editor's existing Apply action) calls `window.api.applyResource(yaml)` and shows success/error via the existing toast system (S33)
A 'Close' or 'Clear' button resets the editor content and collapses the drawer
The drawer state (open/closed, height) is local component state — no Zustand changes required
The bottom drawer does not interfere with the existing right-side detail/YAML panel used for editing existing resources
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Implement the drawer as a new component `src/renderer/src/components/BottomDrawer.tsx`. Use a resize handle div with onMouseDown to implement drag-to-resize (track mouse movement in a document-level mousemove listener, clean up on mouseup). The YAML skeleton template should be a simple constant string. Reuse the Monaco editor already present in the codebase — do not add a second editor library.

stories.title: Remove New resource button from PodsView
stories.description: The PodsView component currently has a 'New' or 'Create' button for creating a new pod resource. Pods are not typically created directly — they are managed by controllers (Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.). Remove this button from the PodsView toolbar.
acceptance_criteria: The 'New' / 'Create' button is removed from `src/renderer/src/components/PodsView.tsx`
Any state variables, handlers, or dialog components used exclusively by that button (e.g. create dialog open state, createPod handler) are also removed
All other pod functionality (Logs button, YAML editor, Delete button, table listing) remains unaffected
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes

stories.title: Remove New resource button from all resource view components
stories.description: Audit every resource view component in `src/renderer/src/components/` and remove any 'New' / 'Create' button that opens a create-resource dialog. The bottom drawer (S37) is the single entry point for creating new resources going forward. This story supersedes S38 (which only targeted PodsView) and covers all views.
acceptance_criteria: Every file matching `src/renderer/src/components/*View.tsx` is checked for a 'New' or 'Create' toolbar button
Any such button — and all state variables, dialog open/close handlers, and create-dialog JSX used exclusively by it — is removed from each affected component

The following views are confirmed clean after the change: DeploymentsView, DaemonSetsView, StatefulSetsView, ServicesView, IngressesView, PodsView, ConfigMapsView, SecretsView, ReplicaSetsView, NodesView, NamespacesView
All other functionality in each view (YAML editor, Delete button, detail panel, table listing) remains unaffected
No unused imports are left behind from the removed code
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: S38 already removed the New button from PodsView; verify it is gone and apply the same removal to any remaining views that still have it. Do not remove create-related IPC handlers from the main process — only the UI buttons and dialogs are in scope.

stories.title: Move pod Logs button from list view to detail panel
stories.description: The 'Logs' button currently appears in every pod row in the PodsView table (added by S34). Move it into the pod detail panel so it is only visible when a pod row is selected and the detail panel is open. The log-tailing functionality itself (PodLogPanel, IPC handlers) remains unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The 'Logs' (ScrollText) button is removed from every pod row in `src/renderer/src/components/PodsView.tsx`
A 'Logs' button (ScrollText icon, same visual style as before) is added to the pod detail panel header or action bar, visible when a pod is selected
Clicking the Logs button in the detail panel opens `PodLogPanel` exactly as it did before — replacing the detail content with the live log stream
The 'Close' / 'Stop' controls in PodLogPanel return the user to the pod detail view (not a blank panel)
When no pod is selected, no Logs button is visible anywhere in PodsView
All other pod row actions (YAML editor, Delete button) remain in the row as-is
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes

stories.title: Move pod log view to bottom drawer
stories.description: The PodLogPanel currently renders in the right-hand detail area of PodsView. Move it to a persistent bottom drawer (like the existing BottomDrawer component) so the log stream is visible while the user continues to interact with the pod list and detail panel above. The drawer slides up from the bottom of the app window and can be resized or closed.
acceptance_criteria: PodLogPanel no longer renders inside the PodsView right-hand detail area; the detail panel remains visible when a pod is selected
A bottom drawer component renders at the app layout level (not inside PodsView) so it overlays/pushes all views
Clicking the Logs button on a selected pod opens the bottom drawer and starts the log stream for that pod
The bottom drawer has a visible header showing the pod name and container selector (if multi-container)
The drawer has a Close button that stops the log stream and collapses the drawer
The drawer has a resize handle so the user can drag it to change its height
Log content scrolls and auto-scrolls to bottom unless user has manually scrolled up, same behaviour as before
Only one log stream is active at a time; opening logs for a different pod stops the previous stream and starts the new one
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Reuse or extend the existing BottomDrawer component at `src/renderer/src/components/BottomDrawer.tsx`. Lift bottom-drawer state (open, podName, namespace, container) into the Zustand app store so PodsView can trigger it without prop drilling. The drawer should be rendered in App.tsx at the root layout level.

stories.title: Namespace filter with persistent selection
stories.description: Add a namespace selector dropdown to the AppBar. The selected namespace is stored in the Zustand app store and applies to all namespace-scoped resource views (Pods, Deployments). When the user switches between resource types the namespace selection is preserved. An 'All Namespaces' option shows unfiltered results.
acceptance_criteria: AppBar renders a namespace selector dropdown next to the context selector; it lists all namespaces fetched from the cluster
Dropdown includes an 'All Namespaces' option as the default selection
Zustand store holds `selectedNamespace: string | null` where `null` means all namespaces
PodsView filters the displayed pods to match `selectedNamespace`; when null, all pods across all namespaces are shown
DeploymentView (and any other namespace-scoped list view) filters the same way using the same store value
Switching tree-view selection (e.g. from Pods to Deployments) keeps the current namespace selection unchanged
Changing the context (cluster) resets `selectedNamespace` to null
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Reuse the existing `k8s:namespaces:list` IPC handler to populate the dropdown. The namespace selector should sit between the context selector and any cluster-type badge in the AppBar. Filter logic lives in the renderer — pass `selectedNamespace` into each resource view and filter the list before rendering.

stories.title: Apply namespace filter to additional resource views
stories.description: Extend the namespace filter introduced in S43 to the remaining namespace-scoped resource list views: Services, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, and Secrets. Each view must read `selectedNamespace` from the Zustand store and filter its list accordingly, consistent with the pattern already applied to Pods and Deployments.
acceptance_criteria: ServicesView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
ReplicaSetsView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
StatefulSetsView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
DaemonSetsView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
IngressesView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
ConfigMapsView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
SecretsView filters displayed rows by `selectedNamespace`; when null, all namespaces shown
Switching between any of these views preserves the current namespace selection
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Filter logic is renderer-side only — no new IPC handlers needed. Each view reads `useAppStore(s => s.selectedNamespace)` and applies `.filter(r => selectedNamespace === null || r.metadata?.namespace === selectedNamespace)` before rendering the table.

stories.title: Refactor bottom drawer to tabbed multi-panel
stories.description: Merge PodLogDrawer and BottomDrawer into a single unified tabbed bottom drawer. Any content that opens in the bottom drawer — pod logs, new resource forms, or future panel types — appears as a tab. Multiple tabs can be open simultaneously. The user can switch between tabs, close individual tabs, and the drawer collapses when all tabs are closed.
acceptance_criteria: A single `BottomDrawer` component at app root level replaces all existing bottom-drawer and pod-log-drawer components
Each panel (pod log, new resource form, etc.) opens as a new tab inside the drawer; tabs show a label (e.g. pod name for logs, resource kind for new-resource forms)
Clicking an already-open tab's trigger (e.g. Logs button for the same pod) switches focus to that tab rather than opening a duplicate
Each tab has an individual close (×) button; closing the last tab collapses the drawer
The drawer resize handle works as before — dragging changes height for all tabs
Pod log tabs: header shows pod name + container selector; log stream starts when tab becomes active and stops when tab is closed
Active log streams for non-focused tabs continue running in the background so no data is lost
Zustand store holds `drawerTabs: DrawerTab[]` and `activeTabId: string | null`; opening a panel dispatches an `openDrawerTab` action
Old `BottomDrawer.tsx` and any separate pod-log-drawer file are removed; no dead code remains
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Define a discriminated union `DrawerTab = { id, type: 'pod-log', namespace, podName, container } | { id, type: 'new-resource', resourceKind }` in the store. The tabbed drawer renders the correct panel component based on `tab.type`. Use shadcn/ui Tabs (or a custom tab bar if shadcn Tabs don't fit the bottom-drawer layout) for the tab strip.

stories.title: Name filter input beside namespace selector
stories.description: Add a text input field to the AppBar, placed beside the namespace selector, that filters all resource list views by resource name. The filter matches any resource whose `metadata.name` contains the input string (case-insensitive substring match). The filter value is stored in the Zustand app store and applies universally to every resource type shown in the main panel.
acceptance_criteria: AppBar renders a text input field immediately beside the namespace selector dropdown
Input has a placeholder such as 'Filter by name...'
Zustand store holds `nameFilter: string` (empty string means no filter)

Every resource list view (Pods, Deployments, Services, ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Ingresses, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Nodes, Namespaces) reads `nameFilter` from the store and filters rows where `metadata.name` contains the filter string (case-insensitive)
Filter is applied in addition to the namespace filter — both filters are AND-ed together
Switching between resource types preserves the current name filter value
Changing the cluster context resets `nameFilter` to empty string
Clearing the input (empty string) shows all resources unfiltered
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Filter logic is renderer-side only — no new IPC handlers needed. Each view reads `useAppStore(s => s.nameFilter)` and applies `.filter(r => !nameFilter || r.metadata?.name?.toLowerCase().includes(nameFilter.toLowerCase()))` after the namespace filter. Reset `nameFilter` in the same store action that resets `selectedNamespace` on context change.

stories.title: Prometheus endpoint configuration and metrics IPC
stories.description: Allow the user to configure a Prometheus base URL (and optional Bearer token) that the app uses to query pod metrics. The configuration is persisted via Electron's electron-store (or a plain JSON config file in userData). Expose IPC handlers in the main process that query Prometheus range queries for CPU, memory, network, and disk metrics for a given pod.
acceptance_criteria: A settings entry stores `prometheusUrl: string` and `prometheusToken: string` (optional); defaults to empty strings
A settings UI (modal or dedicated settings section reachable from the AppBar) lets the user enter and save the Prometheus base URL and optional Bearer token
IPC handler `prometheus:config:get` returns `{ prometheusUrl, prometheusToken }`
IPC handler `prometheus:config:set` accepts `{ prometheusUrl, prometheusToken }` and persists the values

IPC handler `prometheus:pod:metrics` accepts `{ namespace, podName, step?, rangeMinutes? }` and returns `{ cpu: DataPoint[], memory: DataPoint[], networkRx: DataPoint[], networkTx: DataPoint[], diskRead: DataPoint[], diskWrite: DataPoint[] }` where `DataPoint = { timestamp: number, value: number }`
Queries use Prometheus HTTP API `/api/v1/query_range`; default range is last 30 minutes, step 60s
CPU query: `rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>',container!=''}[5m])`
Memory query: `container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>',container!=''}`
Network Rx: `rate(container_network_receive_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Network Tx: `rate(container_network_transmit_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Disk read: `rate(container_fs_reads_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
Disk write: `rate(container_fs_writes_bytes_total{namespace=~'<ns>',pod='<pod>'}[5m])`
If Prometheus URL is not configured, handler returns an error `{ error: 'Prometheus not configured' }`
If the HTTP request fails, handler returns `{ error: '<message>' }` without crashing the main process
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Use Node's built-in `fetch` (Node 18+) or the `axios` package for HTTP requests in the main process. Store config with `electron-store` package (add to dependencies). Serialize all response data to plain objects before sending over IPC. Sum multi-container series client-side or aggregate with `sum by (pod)` in the PromQL query.

stories.title: Pod metrics graphs in pod detail panel
stories.description: Display CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O metric graphs inside the pod detail panel. When a pod is selected in the resource list, the detail panel shows a 'Metrics' section with four line charts populated via the `prometheus:pod:metrics` IPC handler. Charts auto-refresh every 60 seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Pod detail panel includes a 'Metrics' section below the existing pod info
Four charts are rendered: CPU Usage (cores), Memory Usage (bytes formatted as MiB/GiB), Network I/O (Rx and Tx on same chart), Disk I/O (Read and Write on same chart)
Charts use `recharts` (add to dependencies); each is a `LineChart` with a time-based X axis and labeled Y axis
On mount the component calls `window.api.getPrometheusPodMetrics({ namespace, podName })` and populates the charts
A loading spinner is shown while the request is in flight
If Prometheus is not configured, the Metrics section shows a message 'Prometheus not configured — add URL in Settings'
If the request errors, an inline error message is shown with a retry button
Charts refresh automatically every 60 seconds while the pod detail panel is open
Switching to a different pod cancels the pending refresh and starts a fresh fetch for the new pod
No TypeScript compile errors after the changes
stories.notes: Install `recharts` and `@types/recharts` (if needed). Format bytes on Y axis with a custom tick formatter (`bytes => (bytes / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1) + ' MiB'`). Use `useEffect` with a `setInterval` for auto-refresh; clear interval on unmount. Network chart: two `<Line>` series (Rx = blue, Tx = orange). Disk chart: two `<Line>` series (Read = green, Write = red). Add `window.api.getPrometheusPodMetrics` and `window.api.getPrometheusConfig` / `window.api.setPrometheusConfig` to the preload `contextBridge`.
